title: Establishing a High-Performance and Productive Ecosystem for Distributed Execution of Python Functions Using Globus Compute
problem: Users face significant barriers bridging high-level Python workloads and HPC systems, including authentication, network management, and software deployment. Inefficiencies remain in wrapping external applications (C/C++, Fortran, MPI) where users must deploy multiple endpoints to exploit different configurations.
motivation: Democratizing access to heterogeneous research computing resources is essential for accelerating research progress in an increasingly diverse ecosystem.
method: Globus Compute is enhanced with three key components: (1) an asynchronous, future-based executor interface for task submission and monitoring, (2) shell and MPI-based function types to wrap external applications transparently, and (3) a multi-user endpoint architecture that allows administrators to deploy single endpoints shared by authorized users.
key_novelty: Multi-user endpoint architecture enabling a single deployment to serve multiple authorized users with different needs, eliminating the previous requirement to deploy multiple endpoints per configuration.
contributions: Asynchronous, future-based executor interface for task submission and monitoring
Shell and MPI-based function types for wrapping external applications
Multi-user endpoint capability enabling shared resource access
Integrated ecosystem reducing barriers between Python and HPC resources
primary_theme: Distributed Python function execution for HPC systems
